chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl narrated from ʿUqbah ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who said to his wife, “O adulteress.”
He عليه السلام said: “He is to be flogged as a hadd punishment, and they are to be separated after he has been flogged, and she will no longer be his wife.”
He عليه السلام said: “But if he said words that slipped out from him without knowing anything, intending thereby only to anger her, then they are not to be separated.”

key_terms.أَفْلَتَ مِنْهُ: it slipped out from him unintentionally
key_terms.حَدًّا: a fixed legal punishment under sacred law
key_terms.يَا زَانِيَةُ: an accusation of adultery directed at the wife
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: he is to be flogged with the prescribed punishment
key_terms.يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَهُمَا: the spouses are to be separated

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man says to his wife, "O adulteress"?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a husband who accuses his wife of zina. It states that if the accusation is made in a binding manner, he is punished and the spouses are separated, while if the statement merely slipped out in anger without knowledge, separation does not occur.
